utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yesterday I asked you on purpose whether the appearance of the crater at Dobrinja was typical or not. You said it was a typical appearance. There was a stabiliser but it was not covered in rubble. Would this type of material be able to return to the crater on its own spontaneously, as it were?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I believe that the ground in the market was similar to the surface of the footpath. Judging by the photos from the photo file, this is a pebble foundation covered by a layer of asphalt, and I believe that the surfaces in both cases were very similar. What I said yesterday about the typical surface meant the following: When a body penetrates a surface at a high speed, the material of the ground has to be pushed out by the penetrating body and it has to be either in the vicinity of the place where the high-velocity-speed body penetrated or it has to be scattered by the shock wave, although the shock wave precedes the very event. Let's be clear on one thing, the process that occurs during an explosion follows the following sequence: A projectile hits the surface, it is activated, and then the explosive is activated because it has to reach a certain pressure for the casing to be expanded and broken. At that moment there is an explosion and the fragments of the casing scatter and the shock wave exerts destructive activity in the vicinity. When the casing is fragmented, the rear of the projectile is also fragmented, and that includes the stabiliser. Depending on the velocity of the projectile, the stabiliser either continues flying towards the point of the explosion in the nearby area or becomes embedded if its speed is higher than the speed of its rejection from the projectile. If it is not higher, i.e., if the speed is less than the speed of the projection from the projectile, it falls somewhere around in the vicinity of the point of explosion or it is pushed backwards in the direction of the incoming trajectory. In this case, we would expect a totally different appearance of the crater. We would expect for the surroundings of the crater were littered with soil, pebbles, asphalt, everything else that may have been pushed out by the embedding of the stabiliser, whereas the stabiliser is either partially or fully visible like it was in the crater that we saw yesterday. In technical terms, this is completely inexplicable.

utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, 67 and 68. We have just compared 64 with 66 and now I want to compare 67 and 68.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us something about these two images? How come the first crater looks the way it does and the other looks differently? The vicinity of the two craters is different. The material looks different. Can you tell us something about the craters, the stabiliser?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The image --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: These questions are extremely leading, this last one certainly was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Doctor, could you please tell us what the characteristics of the two craters are? Can you tell us something about the material that surrounds them? Can you tell us something about the bottom of the crater and the appearance of the stabiliser?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Image 67 depicts the penetration of a stabiliser into the footpath. This happened on the 4th of February in Dobrinja, a day earlier. The appearance is very characteristic. The material has been pushed out, and you can see that around the penetration point the material is pushed out and the stabiliser is completely embedded, but it is almost fully visible. This is an expected appearance in view of the process that I just described. This is an expected appearance of a crater after such a penetration. Image 68 depicts a crater at Markale and here we can see that it must have been dug out, which means that you could not reach it if it hadn't been dug out. And you can tell that by the material that has been taken out of that crater. And also, we can see that there are two asphalt levels under which the crater is buried. In the previous image we saw that it was completely invisible. The material has clearly been dug out, but this is impossible. Let me be more clear. Something like that could happen only if we were to throw things into the water and the water would then close above it. This is solid matter and an appearance like this is impossible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please mark the two layers with an electronic pen. You have mentioned the two layers or the two levels of asphalt. Can you please mark them with an electronic pen.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And, Doctor, by "previous image," did you mean figure 66?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. You can't see anything in that image if this is what you meant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please put today's date and initial the image. And now I would like to call up image 72 to replace image 67 on the left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll receive this separately.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D3546, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Image 72, can I have it on the left-hand side. In the Serbian version of the document it's on page 99. Can you tell us what the image represents? How come that the air spaces between the tail fins are larger than in image 68?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a frame from the video-clip which was recorded on the 6th of February by the police. We got this image from Mr. Zecevic. This is P6361 from the Slobodan Milosevic case. The image shows the stabiliser that Mr. Zecevic returned into the crater. According to his statement, he just lowered it down and he measured the angle of descent. That's why everything is so very well visible and clear in this image. You can see the gravel or little stones with which he fixated that stabiliser so it would remain in this position. And if you want me to do so, I can mark the gravel that's fixed the stabiliser. This only means that the opening was much bigger than the stabiliser itself because the stabiliser had to be fixed in a certain position. I suppose that I don't even have to say that the fixing of the stabiliser is an arbitrary activity that any one of us could fix an object in a larger space as whichever way we want to do that. This is also seen in the film that was taken by the police on that day. However, interestingly enough - and I have to mention that - is that the film shows in great detail the place of explosion starting with 1300 hours up to nearly 1400 hours, and you can see clearly that the place of explosion is completely covered. And then there is a break of some 20 to 30 minutes in that film, and then what appears is the image that we are looking at now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We are going to see the film in a minute, but before that can you tell us if a stabiliser is fixed with a pebble and if it is moved by a certain degree. What would be the resulting aberration in an area of some 4 to 5 kilometres?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have to consult firing tables in order to be able to answer your question. However, the -- any change in the angle of descent changes the place from which the shell was launched. I could tell you exactly if I were to consult my firing tables or if I were to give an access to documents during the break, then I would be able to tell you whether it's 500 or a thousand metres.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to show the video under 1D7441 from the beginning to 8 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This happened on the 6th of February; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the 6th of February, yes -- well, this is what my colleague Zecevic marked. You can see that the stabiliser cannot be seen although it has been zoomed in, and that was at 1319 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now can we see what happened between 9.00 and 9.30?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My colleague marked it here. There it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we stop it?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mr. President, I just want to make sure that an error does not get embedded in the record. Mr. Karadzic in his question said, "This happened on the 6th of February; right?" Now, it's clear from even the title of the witness's report that the incident happened on the 5th of February and the filming took place on the 6th of February. I know Mr. Karadzic was obviously not trying to mislead the Chamber in that respect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I understood that way, yes. The filming took place on 6th of February; that's what you meant?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. In the video the date is the 6th of February, 1994, and I wanted to draw the participants' attention to the fact that it was not filmed on the 5th, but rather on the 6th.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, that's the image which is included in the report and it can be quite clearly seen that the small stones were used to fix the position in the crater which is much larger and did not exist an hour earlier or half an hour earlier in the same video and that the place within the crater is fixed with the small stones from left to right. There are, well, five. And as I said, at the beginning of the video we could clearly see that the crater was not there at all, or rather, that it was buried with rubble. And on the basis of that, it can be concluded that my colleague Mr. Zecevic did not just lower the stabiliser in the existing crater, but that the crater was made after -- immediately after the stabiliser was lowered into the crater.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this identical with image 72 from your report?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Actually, this is the image.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you also tell us why is there no dust between the wings and why is this wider than in figure 60 --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's quite obvious. A bigger and wider crater was made in which the stabiliser was later lowered, and there was no reason for the existence of the dust in the wider crater. And it's obvious that the stabiliser is fixed with the small stones which are also quite clearly visible in this video because the video is good.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I tender these two extracts from 0 to 8 and from 9.00 to 9.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, any objections?

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: No. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. So is it an excerpt from an already-existing exhibit? We didn't admit Zecevic's video.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Your Honour, to be perfectly honest, I think this is part of a video which we have played. Now, I don't know if these specific parts have been admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But for clarity, we'll admit it separately.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D3547, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Both extracts can be under one number; right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we now please look at figure 74.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us, thanks to this image and the series of images, what can be concluded on the basis of the examination of the stabiliser? Figure 74 and 75, please. We can depict them on the whole screen, I mean we can zoom in and remove this.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the stabiliser which as a piece of evidence relating to the Markale evidence on the 5th of February is present here, in this Tribunal. And the following can be noticed with regard to it. I just have to mention for a second a fact because of which I will discuss the stabiliser, namely it's the following: In his report and opinion, my colleague Mr. Zecevic, together with his commission, concluded, or rather, determined the angle of descent on the basis of the stabiliser which we just saw and which embedded into the ground, according to his claim, and allowed him to determine the angle of descent. First of all, the method which my colleague Mr. Zecevic used is inexistent to this day, 15 years later, because such a method would be the result of a stochastic process in which we cannot suppose what the margin of error is if we were to use it as the method. The method depends on a series of parameters, and I will just list the crucial ones. In order to be at least approximately exact, then the breaking of the stabiliser --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the witness please slow down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Was I too fast again?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Interpreters didn't hear after you said, "In order to be at least approximately exact ..."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In order for the method to be at least approximately exact, it is necessary for several criteria to be met, namely, the severing at the moment when the stabiliser is thrown away would have to be axisymmetric with regard to the cross-section and with regard to the longitudinal axis, which can be clearly seen from image 74. That was not the case because the severance was not axisymmetric. And another thing that would be necessary --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If I may ask you because of technical terms the interpreters are having some trouble, so if you can please slow down as much as possible. You said that it was excentric. So the --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The way it's severed is excentric with regard to the longitudinal axis, which is clearly seen in figure 74. Another criteria that would have to be met is that the ground has to be homogenous, which means that it would have to be uniform rather than varying in terms of how compact it is and what are the sizes of the stones, that there is asphalt which is a different kind of ground and a different kind of material. So this criterion hasn't been met either. And finally, another criterion that would have to be met, the effect of the shock wave would have to be completely symmetrical, the shock wave of the explosive charge which can never be uniformly repeated, regardless of how much we might try to make the casing so that it breaks in one moment in all places. And regardless of how our colleagues who are in charge of producing explosives may try to make the explosive fully homogenous and repetitive by all its characteristics. So each explosive wave which is produced during the explosion of a piece of ordnance is something that cannot be repeated, simply because technologically we cannot achieve this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you need the lower two figures if you are to continue with the description of this?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. All this had to do with figure 74. If we look at figure 75, we see something that is seriously illogical, namely, that on the fins of this stabiliser there are some traces, traces of penetration and traces of damage caused by the material through which the stabiliser pass. What is illogical here is that on the body of the stabiliser there is not a single trace of penetration and it was the part that penetrated first under the condition that the stabiliser was found at the spot where we saw it on the previous photographs and in the following manner: The shell exploded and it penetrated into the ground. All of this seems to indicate -- first, what is down here indicates the fact that it did not find itself in its crater in this way, and the upper figure seems to indicate that such a method cannot be used to determine the angle of descent not even an approximation of it. And we never verified it as a method precisely for this reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What were the ways in which the stabiliser could have ended up in this position?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean in the crater?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, in the crater and in the furrow.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on the physical traces which we have looked at already, the shape of the crater is not characteristic, not only that it's not typical, it's physically impossible. It couldn't have been like this. By penetrating through such ground and to have the crater look as it does with such an appearance, that wouldn't have been possible. We really analysed this in detail. Could it have flown to the Markale market to the location where it was determined it landed? We tried to confirm it on the basis of physical parameters, namely, the shape of the stalls, the dimensions of the stalls, the distribution of the stalls, and the physical location of the explosion, that is to say the location at which the explosion occurred.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could we now please see figure 80 so that we can see how Mr. Zecevic depicted the stall and then we'll find the sketch of the actual stall. So figure 80 is the one that we need now. Is this sketch of the stall correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We have seen the videos and we can say that it's not correct. The stall doesn't look like this at all. The only thing that we accepted as correct is the width of the counter and also the height which Mr. Zecevic measured and the sketch is incorrect if we compare it with the videos that we watched. We asked both Mr. Sabljica and Mr. Zecevic why the stall is depicted like this; however, Mr. Sabljica said that he just took it over from Mr. Zecevic, he took over the sketch, and Mr. Zecevic replied, as far as I remember, that such a shape of the stall was taken in order to prove that the shell landed or something similar to this. And I have no opinion about the reply because I don't understand it. But in any case, we used it to reconstruct the actual shape and dimensions of the stall on the basis of the videos and these two measured values which I just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we now please look at image 82. And if we could keep the previous one on the left half of the screen and have the other one on the right. Or perhaps you can just explain it to us, we don't have to compare. Is this sketch of the stall correct and truthful?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a truthful reconstruction of the stall because the height as measured by Mr. Zecevic has been adopted here and I previously said that by the use of the video recordings we determined the proportions, the angles, and all the necessary geometrical elements which we needed in order to determine the actual shape and dimensions of the stall, the dimensions in the first place. And what you called up in e-court now is actually a depiction of the possibility, or rather, the impossibility of the shell landing where it turned out to be because you see X equals 1 metre. That's the distance from the stall counter to the impact point measured by Mr. Zecevic's commission, and once all the checks are done we can see that the shell could only have landed along the direction marked with number 2, that is to say at a distance of 1.37 metres from the stall counter and not in any case at a distance of just 1 metre from the stall counter without hitting the roof of the stall.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we see figure 6 just for a moment, please, page 36 in the Serbian language. Could you explain these angles for us, please.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. The angles are taken over from the video. Let me just see what the figure is. It's figure number 3 taken from the video recording made by the police. We measured in AutoCAD the angles and we then made a reconstruction of the stall. Now, of course we measured 66.49 and 65.22 because that's the locksmith's work, so we worked with the angle of 65 which was probably correct. The proportions and the distances between the ground and the first cross-beam and the height of the counter, these proportions were determined on the basis of figure number 5 in AutoCAD, and then it was recalculated so as to arrive at the actual dimensions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So in figure 82, the lines 1 and 2 must follow or do they follow the angle? How did you arrive at the direction and what angle of descent do these lines follow? You told us that one couldn't have landed at just 1 metre distance from the stall. If we can go back to image 82, please. Which angle do lines 1 and 2 tally with? What is the angle of descent?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was verified -- my apologies. I need a sip of water. This was verified in terms of the maximum angle as determined by Mr. Zecevic, 65, from the azimuth of 23, not 18. Let me just say that the situation is far more unfavourable when the azimuth is 18, and just to remind you we determined the azimuth of 23 as the base line anticipated line of azimuth based on the traces retrieved on the wall of the UPI 101 building which can be seen in the background.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you mention the possibility of it being a statically activated explosion?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of all the analysis we did - and we did very complex analysis - we even assessed what the minimum angle would be in respect of the point of impact in relation to the position of the stall. We did all the various checks we could based on the information available to us, and I think we went beyond our call of duty. We concluded that there was no possibility for the shell landing in that point and being activated there without hitting the roof of the stall in the process. The only possibility for the shell to be activated at the point where it was was for it to have been statically activated, or rather, that the shell was statically activated in a certain position at a certain site. There is no other technical explanation. We explored and checked all the possibilities that were the parameters restricting the possibility for the mine to land there, and all these checks returned with a result which said that this was impossible. And we mentioned all these various explanations in the report. There is a stall and there is an indication that an explosion may have occurred beneath the stall, but I do stand by my position that the shell could not have landed and impacted in the spot where it did without having first hit the roof of the stall.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us which figure it is which indicates the possibility that the shell was activated beneath a stall?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. I had it a moment ago. That's figure 69.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have figure 69 shown, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what should be observed in this figure?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the stall indicated by this journalist, whomever he is, that the stall was overturned by 180 degrees, which means that the explosion happened in front of it and it upturned it. What is on the bottom is the roofing panel of the stall, and above the head of the person indicating this we can see the portion of the stall which shows soot from the explosion and a bit is missing here. The experts who concluded that the explosion took place on the stall must have been confused by the fact that the stall is upturned as it is. However, it is quite evident that what is now lying on the ground is the roofing panel of the stall because you can see the part of the stall in line with the head. We can see the frame, the central supports of the stall which are now lying down on the surface of the ground -- or perhaps you want me to mark it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That would not be a bad idea.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I ask the usher to activate the pen for Dr. Subotic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 1 is the damaged counter of the stall. We can see its bottom side.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And what is the position of the stall?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The stall's roofing panel is on the ground. It's marked with D1 on this image as far as I can see it. It's probably to do with a text that somebody drafted in connection with the image.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Had the explosion not taken place under the stall, what would the situation with this stall be?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would have been overturned to the left or to the right if the explosion took place in approximate vicinity. Depends on the shock wave and the exact position.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So instead of being upside down, it would be overturned on its -- lying on its side; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Defence witness Derek Allsop said that he did not support the thesis which indicated that this was a static explosion because the stabiliser could not have become embedded in the ground in that way. What is your opinion of it?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I viewed this testimony and the gentleman is right because he was looking at a specific case. Had the static explosion taken place there and the stabiliser been positioned on the shell, then it would not have been possible because the shell did not fly in and there would not have been that speed that we referred to. It would not have been possible for the stabiliser to become embedded in the ground. I agree so far. But this implies the fact that a shell complete with a stabiliser is statically activated. That's the only scenario that is being considered here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So what are the other possibilities that would allow for both these options, that the stabiliser would be embedded in the ground and the explosion statically activated?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In -- we wrote this possibility in our expert report, and this is what it is: The stabiliser could have been dug into the surface or the ground previously. It could have been covered over with some material. And then above, with a certain surface and at some angle, a shell without a stabiliser could have been placed and remotely activated. This would be the scenario that would fit completely with what we saw in all these images so far. The crater had to appear the way it did. It wasn't recognisable. The stabiliser was embedded, which was obviously necessary in order to prove that the shell had flown in with a large charge. I also saw that the Defence witness said that it was impossible to bury the stabiliser in previously before the shell is activated because then the crater would become widened, but that would only happen if the shell was placed directly on that surface. In that case, what he said would indeed happen; however, he did not take into consideration the scenario that I'm discussing, and that is that the shell could have been placed on a surface of its own. And this could have easily have been a wooden plank. If you paid attention to the figures that we looked at, we had a wreath produced by the shock wave which was wider than your normal central crater. You will have seen that I marked these two levels with numbers 1 and 2. The situation you here is as if it had been somehow compressed down, and that is not your normal appearance of a central crater produced by an incoming shell which is activated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this image be admitted as a separate exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can I have your date and signature, please.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see the time and I leave it in your hands to decide when the break will be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll admit this.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D3548, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll have a break and resume at three past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Doctor, can I ask you to make corrections if you have them ready before we finish this topic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Did this document receive a number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Well, we haven't quite heard the corrections yet, but as a general matter no objections to the admission of the report.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: I am talking about this exhibit that is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Oh, yeah. Have we not admitted as 3548?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I will tender the entire document after the corrections have been made and after we've addressed Markale 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Go ahead, Doctor.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, now over the break I have managed to find in this new document that I received yesterday that it's on page 21, paragraph 1 --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please, others don't have the same copy.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. It's paragraph 75, I believe. Yes, paragraph 75, subparagraph (b), the title is "angle of descent." So it's -- actually, I apologise, sub-item (c), "crater." It's a rather long paragraph, I apologise. Somewhere in the middle, approximately, of the second paragraph it reads: "Or partly visible item 48, figure 67. In figure 68 one can see the extent of material that was," there's a word here which was a typo and which should read, "which was necessary to dig out."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is correct in English.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right. That was important because the word doesn't have any meaning the way it is. Now, the same paragraph, subparagraph (d), there's quite a few of them, I'm sorry, at the top of page 122 it reads: "Since the CSB Sarajevo and Berko Zecevic's commission established that the shell landed at a distance of 1 metre from the edge of the stall counter, a line was drawn parallel at a distance of 1 metre from the stall, figure 82." And it says "which touches upon the edge of the stall," whereas it should say that it is tangential to the roof of the stall. That's the third line at the top of page 122.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters note we didn't find it in the original.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It's in the middle of the page in the English "since the CSB ...," the sentence finishes with "figure 68."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: This is just middle of the page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The sentence before the text that is in bold.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Doctor, would that (d) be (e)?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. It was automatic numbering and that's perhaps how the error came about, and then everything should of course be readjusted because I do believe that paragraph (e) follows after this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I don't think that there is an (e), so could we perhaps put it down as (e) static explosion.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Anything else, Doctor?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, that will be all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we finish off the issue of Markale 1 with the following question: Is there anything else in the material available which would confirm, reinforce, or detract from your position that it was a static explosion? And I'm not just referring to the ballistics but the entire circumstances surrounding the incident. Is there anything out of the ordinary in the documentation which would be contrary to your position that there was this sort of manipulation? If you could list these items, if any.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With permission, this is what I will say. Based on the material and all the documents we reviewed, we established that there were many events and actions which indicated that the incident did not occur all at once or in some sort of natural process. The TV filming began immediately after the incident happened. This was obvious to be seen because we saw people running out of the market-place with shopping bags in hand and there was manipulation on the side of Dzenetica Cikma Street which is a small street and it's an impassable one. The vehicles were moving along Marsala Tita Street in the opposite direction to the one regulated. We saw individuals wearing official insignia. All of this was filmed by the cameras that were there in an instant. We know that the police arrived almost before the evacuation started. All of this was quite unusual, quite unexpected. The entire evacuation was completed within 15 minutes and we know that there were quite a few people -- quite a few casualties. It is of course quite understandable that there was such wide media coverage of it. I will not even go into that in detail. However, we did observe that shortly afterwards there were manipulations with the numbers of victims and we did present this in detail in our expert report. And something that we were able to observe from the documents that we reviewed was that on the following day with a cover letter from the United Nations some 40-odd, I think 42, injured persons were sent out. When we compared the lists, on that particular list there were only 12 who were on the list of the injured at Markale itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we pause here. I just -- although this part cannot be related to the expertise of Dr. Subotic, but I just let it go because it might be related to witness's credibility as well. But, Doctor, when you said "we," who did you mean by "we"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I say "we," I mean myself and my associates who worked hard with me in the collection and analysis of the material that I listed in the document and my associates were named in the document, that's Mr. Poparic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Please continue, Mr. Karadzic. MR. KARADZIC [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's just see this page 37, line 7, it turns out that you said that the police arrived almost before the evacuation started. But I believe that you said that the police arrived almost before the evacuation was completed or after the evacuation.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that the police arrived at a point when the evacuation was almost complete. The documents do indicate the time of the arrival of the police as well as the time of the completion of the evacuation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. One other question. You say that 40-odd were sent out. Where exactly were they sent?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. They were sent out to the United States for medical treatment. I think that there were 40 family members and roughly the same number of those who were injured at the market-place in Markale. I think that Akashi drafted the letter. Don't ask me who was in charge of the letter; we do have it cited in the document. We then compared these lists and the list of persons sent out for medical treatment to the United States contained only 12 persons who were injured at Markale.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And from the point of view in ballistic terms, in view of the angle of descent, the obstacles, the propagation of the wave and fragments, how do you account for or explain the number of injured and dead as reported by the Muslim side and as adopted by, of course, the Prosecution in this case?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is controversial data. We systemised that in a table depicting the number of casualties, the dead, and the wounded from this incident. All of these numbers that are represented as official numbers in my view surpasses the technical capabilities of this asset for a simple reason: According to the analysis and measurements that we carried out when this type of asset was developed, its lethal capacity was limited, it would all depend on the number of people who were there; at the moment we provided the analysis of that in this document. So I suppose that the Trial Chamber will be able to look at our method and what aspects were considered in our analysis. What I would like to mention at this point in time is the fact that during our analysis of video recordings we considered something which was confirmed by our colleague Zecevic, and that was yet another explosion site at Markale. He signed that during his testimony. It is my impression that the increased number of casualties was the result of two explosions, not just one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The second explosion that you referred to, was it the result of a mortar shell? Is there proof of the origin of the second explosion?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That second explosion is not referred to in any of the investigators' reports or the documents that we analysed. When we analysed the video recordings, we found traces on the street that connects Dzenetica Cikma Street and the Marsala Tita Street, and on a red stall we found fragments or a fragment pattern and that was in the vicinity, and our colleague Zecevic agreed that that was indeed the point of impact.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Doctor, I would like to move to G19 incident which happened on the 28th of August, 1995, and that case is a -- notorious under the name of Markale 2. Could you please give us the characteristics of that incident in a nutshell and all that based on the physical evidence that you had at your disposal.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before I move to that incident, I would like to apologise to the Trial Chamber for my delay. I went to see a doctor yesterday --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Not for the delay, the interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- for the cough. I went to see a doctor yesterday who diagnosed me with bronchitis which is why I have difficulties in speaking today and frequent bouts of cough.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Doctor, if you at any time would like to have a break, don't hesitate to let us know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course. Thank you for this. If at all necessary, I will certainly address you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In a nutshell, can you tell us what happened there and what was said to have happened during G19 incident on the 28th of August, 1995. We will show images and elements from your report according to your suggestions.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on the investigations of the incident that were carried out, on that day some 200 metres away from that place four shells exploded and according to the same investigations and the results thereof, one of them fell in front of the market on the pavement and killed and injured quite a large number of people. The traces that we found when we analysed the photos that were taken by the CSB were the foundation for our analysis but there were some other documents we managed to obtain with regard to this case; for example, UNPROFOR investigations and UNPROFOR reports. These documents do not indicate that that was indeed the case. They determined the lower angle of descent which was 67 degrees, and we agreed with that as a base line. It was based on the point of impact and the trajectory that the shell had when overflying a building. There were two trajectories that were established and the discrepancy between them is about 10 degrees. One was established by the French Battalion and the other was established by the investigators of the CSB together with UNPROFOR, I suppose. And that was confirmed by Mr. Higgs. We established that his confirmation was erroneous. In any case, there were two trajectories which can be argued because one of them is correct. And we have an interesting phenomenon at play here. There is a surplus of stabiliser in this investigation. In the video-clips we can see two stabilisers who were marked during the investigation by numbers 12 and 13. They were not fixated. One of them was fixated, the other was not. And in my view there was also a stabiliser which is now at the Tribunal which does not correspond to any of the two stabilisers in the video-clip. I would like to say that one of the two stabilisers was never shown in the investigation. And finally, what I have to mention is the fact that an erroneous conclusion was drawn during the analysis of ballistic trajectories when it was said that the radar that was tasked with registering or recording the incoming of the shell did not register this trajectory or the shell coming in. And I'm afraid that this was a serious error that was done during the analysis and during the reporting on the incident. It was said that the trajectory went under the radar beam by consulting the firing table. This -- it is a fact that this would be impossible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you for this summary of the incident, and now I would like to go through some of the details. First of all, can you please tell us what was alleged about the fatal shell, which one of them was in a sequence of the five?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I could understand the documents, it was the fifth consecutive shell, but there are statements to that effect. There are -- 75 statements were taken from witnesses and UNPROFOR members. None of them heard the launch of any of the shells or any of the explosions resulting from those shells. And since the point of explosion or all of the points of explosions are within the radius of 100 to 200 metres, they -- the explosions had to be heard. I'm not denying that they actually did explode, but not on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If the shells had exploded within the range of some 200 metres or less, what would have happened to the crowd of people?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose that the people would scatter if they heard that there was an explosion very close to them, that there was shelling going on. This is my only plausible assumption.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's deal with the topics one by one. How was the angle of descent determined? We will see this image 102. This was taken from the documentation of the Ministry of the Interior of Bosnia and Herzegovina as a result of its investigation. Could you please tell us why would the minimum angle of descent be 67? What would happen if it had been 63 or 59, for example?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This minimum angle of descent --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's wait for the image.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 102, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As I've just told you the minimum angle of descent was calculated based on the point of explosion and the height of the building, on a condition that the shell had overshot the building because it had to in order to reach the point of explosion. Otherwise, it would have hit the roof, if the angle was lesser than 67.15, as is indicated in here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now I would like to deal with the trajectory. Could you please help us with the image number. Would it be 101 or something else? No, it's not 101.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Perhaps we should first see the crater which was the basis for determining the trajectory. I believe that this is image 98.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 98, 97 before it as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's first see 97 then and then 98.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Image 97 depicts the point of explosion marked by number 1 before the place was cleaned because the -- before the traces of blood, dust, and other particles were cleaned, those that had resulted from the explosion. And you can see that the crater is very shallow, barely visible. The fragmentation pattern was practically covered up by the dust and barely visible in the image. This was a photo that the CSB took at the point of explosion before the area was cleaned. And now on to 98 --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: When we're talking about this, could I please ask you to tell us how do you account for the fact that the following images after the cleaning depict more traces of blood in the crater itself than before the cleaning operation took place?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean image 98; right? What image do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: There are other images which depict more traces of blood.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps the place was not well cleaned. In image 98 there are chalk markings as well as in image 101. That's why the traces are more visible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The white traces are the places where fragmentation took place and those were marked with chalk.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Based on the characteristics of the crater, how would you -- what would you conclude about the velocity and the distance from which the shell was launched?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We've already spoken about that today. When a shell flies at a low velocity, its stabiliser has a higher speed of ejection than its flying speed, and what happens is what happened here. The resulting crater is shallow and the stabiliser cannot be found at the point of explosion. However, there is another odd thing happening here. The stabiliser, based on traces it is very clear that the flying velocity was very low because the crater was -- is very shallow and the stabiliser was found 29 to 30 metres laterally from the point of explosion according to the sketch. And this is absolutely impossible. If the point of explosion was not tampered with, if the stabiliser was not, for example, kicked by somebody, the stabiliser cannot be found laterally. It can be found at the point of explosion, at the point when the shell landed, or in the direction of the trajectory, but it cannot be found 20 or 30 metres laterally after the explosion took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What is missing is the word "backward, thrown backward."

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the direction from which the shell was launched.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now look at image 98, and can you please tell us who was it who defined the trajectory and the azimuth and how were they determined?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was taken over --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I apologise. Are there more traces of blood here than before?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This has still not been thoroughly cleaned, I would say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Go ahead, please.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We took this over from Mr. Higgs' report and he in his turn had taken that image over from the CSB photo file. His task was to control the azimuth that was determined by the CSB and all the previous investigators. This is his sketch. During the analysis of what he did we established that he had applied a proper method to determine the trajectory; however, he took into account a wrong part of the Marsal Tito Street and a wrong azimuth. You can tell that from image 100.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Before we see that image, could you please tell us whether it is of any significance that those angles are mentioned, 220 and 170, and what trajectories do they indicate?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are adjacent trajectories that he used to determine the azimuth. 220 and 175, those are intermediate results. But what matters is the fact that he determined a wrong azimuth of the street. His azimuth was 275 for Marsal Tito Street and that is correct, but that azimuth of Marsal Tito Street is not correct for the market, for the place where the market is. The place where the market is located, that angle or that azimuth is different and it can be seen in image 99 and it is 255. Again, this was taken from Google Earth and you can see the market-place there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we see 99, please, and then we will go to 100. Doctor, you can call up any image you want.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can see that part better on the sketch or on the map. Mr. Higgs took the azimuth of the Marsala Tita Street at a wrong place and he got the 275 azimuth as a result. We can see on Google Earth the azimuth of the market itself which is 255. If we look at the city map we can see the location where the market is and we can see also how Mr. Higgs marked this and its location. So if you call up the appropriate image, it will be easy to explain it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Figure 100, please. Can the Doctor please receive assistance with the electronic pen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can explain it first and then if necessary we can mark it, too. Mr. Higgs drew the line where it says 275 degrees and that is indeed the direction of Marsala Tita Street; however, the market is in the slanting part ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you show where that part is which is different from Marsala Tita Street by an arrow.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's this section and the market is here. It's this red place, if it's visible now; if not, I can correct it. This is the azimuth shown on the previous image, that's the direction. The azimuth is 255 degrees and Mr. Higgs made an error because he considered the other section of the street and thereby included the error when determining the azimuth and his result was 175 and actually when this is calculated his result is 265.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you draw a line along Titova Street, namely the section that Mr. Higgs believed that the direction of these two streets were identical?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he believed that this was that and he connected it with this line here marked by him. And the section of Marsala Tita Street where the market is located is this other section and I marked here the location of the market.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please put number 1 for Marsala Tita Street and number 2 for the market.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks] You mean Marsala Tita Street where -- in the section of it where the market is or the part where Higgs considered that the market was?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The Higgs is parallel.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You said that I should mark it with 1?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please also include the date and your initials.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Next Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D3549, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: As for other investigations, what were the incoming trajectories that they noted and what was their range for this shell?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The investigations yielded varying results. I said that the French Battalion determined the azimuth as 160 degrees. The CSB claimed in their investigation conducted jointly with UNPROFOR that it was 170 plus/minus 5. And there are several reports in which it is noted that all five shells landed with an azimuth between 220 and 240. The five or four shells that we talked about and this one shell that landed on the market-place. And of course the same report states that the -- all shells were fired in a same salvo, from one and the same barrel, which is impossible. Whoever has any knowledge of ballistics, of mortars, and the flight of such projectiles can clearly see that that was the way they were launched. One shell cannot land 200 metres away or 200 metres closer. What I mean to say is that the range cannot be reduced in such a manner. That was why they provided an explanation which is also technically illogical; namely, that the fifth shell which exploded at the market hit the roof, changed its trajectory because it's clear that its azimuth was 170 or 160 - we'll see what it is before we conclude - and for the others it was 220 to 240. And then this fifth shell changed the trajectory because it hit the roof and landed as it did. That is also impossible for the reason that no one found that there was any damage on the roof, first of all. And secondly, if the shell had hit the wall, it would have activated on the roof. And if it had hit the roof and had not been activated, then it would land and would not activate on the ground either because then its flight would have been unstable. It could not change the trajectory for 50 degrees and then continue flying regularly -- I mean, with the fuse forwards, oriented forwards. So technically speaking, such a report is completely unacceptable.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we look at figure 115, please. While we're waiting for the figure to come up on the screen, Doctor, if the mortar azimuth was 240, could such mortar fire be helpful for a mortar at 160?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, because any fire which is used and whenever a shell hits is used for the correction of the range or the correction of the direction itself. It is used as a sort of test firing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us something about all of these firing trajectories and which one did you rely on considering that Marsala Tita Street moves in a slightly different direction close to the Markale market?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This figure depicts something else. It shows the trajectories from the 150 to 175 azimuths which are drawn here, and these are actually the azimuths within the range of which the CSB findings and the UNPROFOR findings and the findings of the Joint Commission of the UNPROFOR and CSB, actually, and the French Battalion as well and the findings based on the physical evidence which we checked are based. This is drawn like this in order to illustrate an overview of the configuration of the ground where the azimuths are, considering also the ranges analysed in the report with a view of the possibility of setting a mortar on this ground and firing from it. So, as I say, this is something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is there any indication in this figure where the separation lines were or will we discuss that in a different way?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you visit this section of the ground and what did you determine about the possibility of precise targeting of Markale with 120-millimetre mortar?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly, I did visit the ground or the field with a view of examining all the incidents in the area of Sarajevo, including the position where the mortar may have been set. And we concluded that in the whole range of 150 to 175 degrees there is no place where a mortar can be set and fire from it. The only place was at an azimuth of 176 where there is a hillock as noted in the report. However, the traces at the site, the physical traces, indicate that the correct azimuth was actually 160, as calculated by Mr. Higgs as well when his error is included in his report and then a recalculation is appropriately made, which can be shown in figure 101. I think it's rather indicative. It is extracted from the video recording that was filmed during the measurement of the distance between the centre of the explosion and the wall of the market-place and traces of the shock wave effects against the curve are measured.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, could you repeat.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Doctor mentioned figure 101, so if we can please call it up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And, Doctor, please feel free to call up any figure that you need from your report.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In figure 101 -- let us wait for the figure to appear on the screen. There it is. Figure 101 very clearly depicts the -- on the basis of the damage of the shock wave, this is one of the investigators doing the measurements. The yellow line seen on the image is the tape which the investigators used to measure the centre of the explosion from the market, the distance between the two, that is. And in this image we noted the traces of the border or end of the effects of the shock wave to the right. The yellow line is a normal line in relation to the market, and after all that is the trajectory which was determined towards the market that we agree with. And the red line in the centre is assessed to have been the centre of the explosion. If it were about 6 degrees to the left of the yellow line which is used as the normal here, so if we take that the azimuth of the market has been determined, once you've recalculate everything appropriately, then you get the angle of around 6 degrees as a result. So based on the physical traces on the spot, we checked and found out that the French Battalion had actually correctly determined the incoming trajectory and also that Mr. Higgs properly determined it if the correction is included because he had made an error taking into account a wrong curve line. So it was erroneously concluded that the azimuth was around 160 degrees here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In line 21 on page 51, it was said that you marked with number 1 the left and right borders of the shock wave. Did you say both "left and right"?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, both left and right, that's right, number 1 to the left and number 1 to the right in relation to the yellow line. The centre of the explosion is represented by the red line.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. Can you please tell us in terms of the distance the crater and what happens with the stabiliser what charges would be necessary for a shell to land here and how would -- what would happen with the stabiliser with different charges?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With different charges, as we already said, there are three possibilities for the stabiliser: If the shell is launched with a charge which is the base line of 3 or more, then the stabiliser would embed into the ground; if it's launched with the first and the second charges, I mean the first and the second because usually for security reasons the 120-millimetre shell is not launched with a basic charge, so the first and the second charges, then the stabiliser should be found immediately next to the point of impact or it would be propelled backwards along the incoming trajectory. In this case, as I said, the stabiliser was found 29 metres laterally which is technically absolutely unexplainable.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we please show figure 113 to the Doctor, and could you please explain for us what are the ranges of different charges? Figure 113. We also have a radar in this figure so if you can please explain everything that is relevant for this incident.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this incident, as I have already noted, I believe, the report drawn up the international units, a comprehensive report, said that the radar which was turned on for 24 hours and which was set in such a way and had such a task to detect any shell, the ordinate of which is around 550 metres can be detected, this was not accidental. It was done because then in this way the radar was set to detect any shell considering the ordinates and considering the location where the radar was in relation to the centre of the city of Sarajevo. What can be seen in figure 113 are the lower marginal trajectories by charges which would meet the angle of descent that would be higher than the lower marginal trajectory which was determined on the basis of this building. Unfortunately, as the radar did not register the flight, it was not simple to determine whether the shell had flown in over the building or not. My opinion is that this is a serious mistake because this is what was at stake. The analysis was to determine whether there was a trajectory by which the shell could land at that spot and it was found -- yes, it could land there but not with this angle of descent. Judging by that trajectory, the shell would hit the roof of the building. It is said that the trajectory somehow managed to fly below the beam of the radar and we have here the lower marginal trajectories. So no trajectory which is below these trajectories would be depicted in different colours, and depending on different charges each of them would hit the roof. Only with trajectory with ordinates that are higher than these would satisfy the criterion of the marginal incoming trajectory. If anyone had analysed it in this way -- it's obvious that they neglected this angle of descent in their analysis and they drew the conclusion that this trajectory was such that the shell could fly below the radar beam. But it is shown here that such a trajectory actually does not exist.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, would this 120-millimetre shell with the first charge whose ultimate range at an angle of 67 degrees of 900 metres, would it have been registered by the radar beam? In reference to figure 113.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Do you mean the red?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, the first charge, 900 metres.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it would not have been registered because it is within the area controlled by the radar unless --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the witness please repeat what she said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you repeat your answer, Doctor.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This trajectory would be within the area controlled by the radar. It would have been too close.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And on whose territory would it have been based on your knowledge from the material?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would have been under the control -- in the territory under the control of the BH army. I am, however, convinced that this happened so as to hear the firing, or rather, I suppose the sound of the shell being fired would have been heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [In English] If this happened, I suppose. If this happened.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because there were devices which registered the firing by sound.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can you tell us what would have become of this shell 1.700 and would those two distances then have rejected the stabiliser and the stabiliser would not have ended up embedded in the ground, 1.700 and 900?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As you mean the distances? I didn't understand the question. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Had the shell had the first and the second charges, where would the stabiliser have ended and would the second charge have been caught by the radar?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The second charge would have been registered by the radar, as can be seen on this image, that's number 1. As for the second issue, with the second charge the stabiliser would have ended up in the close proximity of the point of impact.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The other charges 3, 4, 5, and 6, would they have been registered by the radar and where would stabiliser have ended?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the charges, 3 through 6, would have been registered by the radar and the stabiliser would be embedded in the ground, in the surface.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now look at what happened at the site. Can we look at figure, or rather, figures from the beginning, the figures depicting the injured. Figure 87 to start with. And can you explain to us which particular moment in time this is and what the image depicts?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the point in time not -- well, yes, immediately after the explosion because there are still the injured there. They have not been evacuated yet. Just as in Markale 1 the filming started immediately. And we can see that they are at a very small distance from the centre of impact of this 120-millimetre shell. It is a bit unusual the way they are positioned, since they are close to the centre, 1 and a half to 2 metres away from the centre of explosions, still they seem to be seated and calling for help.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we see now figure 88.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, we see the same scene, the man at some 2 metres from the centre of explosion in a seated position calling for help. We are talking about image 88, aren't we?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes. Can we look at image 89.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This image is very interesting and technically inexplicable when we consider the technical capabilities of the asset itself. The injury as displayed here cannot be caused by the fragmentation effect of a 120-millimetre shell or of any more destructive projectile than the 120 shell because the effect does not take place in a concentrated cluster so as to remove the significant part of one's body. Another illogical aspect of this image is that there is an exceptionally small amount of blood beneath this man for an injury as devastating as this is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we see the next figure, figure 90.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The next image was also taken out from a film made by the CSB during their investigation. We can see a man lying on the pavement, injured, with a spray on his body and his bag of something that is the result of fragments and their effect, although I must say that the pattern does not look like any splinter pattern but as a spray of pellets. And let me say that the shell within its construction does not contain pellets. Pellets can be found in other types of shells and in defensive hand-grenades. Another illogical aspect to this image is that close to the electricity post or closer to the edge of the pavement - and this is visible in other images from this film - there is a large quantity of shattered glass. Now, if an explosion occurs outdoors, then it is quite normal that large quantities of shattered glass would be propelled inwards, whereas a small quantity of glass close to the building itself would be out on the pavement. This is another matter for which there is no physical explanation from the point of view of my own profession and in terms of physics itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us where in relation to this man is the point of impact and was it logical for him to fall in this particular direction, or would it be more in line with the laws of physics had his position been different? So where was the explosion in relation to him, on top or bottom?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The bottom of the image. And when you look at the video footage of the area surrounding this frame, there is another illogicality, which is that opposite to this position, close to the electricity post, there are penetration defects on the post which are on the side opposite to the point of impact. So they were not caused by the fact that from the direction of the centre of explosion they flew and passed along this side, rather, the direction in which these fragments acted was the opposite one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we look at figure -- so they came from the opposite direction; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They came from the opposite direction. It was along the same line, as it were, but the direction was the opposite one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we look at figure 92. You mentioned the nature of the traces on this bag which seemed to have come from pellets. Can you tell us what can be concluded on the basis of this image?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is another injured person from Markale where you can see the circles made by Dr. Milosavljevic who drew these circles around the pellets or their marks on the stretcher and the person himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have figure 93.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have yet another injured person here who seemed to have been a casualty of a fire-arm rather than the fragments of a shell.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Perhaps my question was not right. When I spoke about the direction into which this person with a bag fell on the ground, my question was: Was his position to be expected and consistent with the centre of the explosion or not?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The shock wave propagates along the radius from the centre of the explosion radially outwards. Of course dominantly it would propagate in the same direction which caused the explosion. However, where the wave comes across an obstacle such as a person or something else, then it is only to be expected that the way the wave propagates, the direction in which it propagates, the wave would actually knock the person down. And contrary to what is expected, the person is lying face with his head towards the centre of the explosion, whereas it would be expected for him to lie in the opposite direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And this is related to figure 90, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, I was referring to the man who was lying down and had this spray of marks on his body and back.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes. Figure 90. Can I now kindly ask you to explain to us what the situation was like with the stabiliser. Based on the analysis, what can be concluded? Can we first look at figure 104. What did they say? Which stabiliser was this?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A moment, please. Let me find the figure. According to the markings indicated in the film, that's to say number 12, this is the sketch of the point of impact and this stabiliser was found 29 metres laterally away from the centre of explosion. And if I recall, it was close to a wall. Perhaps there is an image of it as well, but if I remember correctly, the video footage and the sketch of the scene, it was found right by the wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we have figure 105 on the right-hand side of the screen, please. [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is there a difference in the way the fins of both these stabilisers were flattened? The condition of the stabiliser in terms of it being burned, charred, eroded and in the way its fins are positioned, is it the same or is it different?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on these images, the deformations are similar. That's to say apparently these two stabilisers were photographed from different angles. So I don't want to speak about the deformations of the fins. However, this sort of deformation can be the result of a vehicle driving over the stabiliser and we could produce 20 such deformations, and these fins are made of tin sheets and it's very easy to deform them. However, what we see in image 105 is the stabiliser photographed by the French Battalion. One can clearly see erosion on it. This is something that when it comes to the other stabilisers mentioned and analysed in this particular case cannot be found.
