The erosion is something that is a physical process acting upon the material and cannot happen only with the natural firing of a shell. It is absolutely impossible. This can only occur as the result of the activity of an explosive charge and the physical removal of the material.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we look at figure 107, the stabiliser shown here which the Prosecution has at its disposal, does it indicate any traces of erosion?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Image 107 --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The erosions as seen in the previous photo?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said no, no. However, there is a fracture on this stabiliser. This fracture is typical of the moment when the stabiliser is rejected from the rest of the shell at the moment of explosion. In this case it is completely different from the stabiliser in the position of this Tribunal. As we indicated here, there are the ends which are folded back, whereas the stabiliser doesn't show that we saw it. We took a photo of it, and this is a stabiliser which -- I apologise, there is a stabiliser in figure 106. Please bear with me. There are traces of erosion, but the fracture does not look the same as the fracture on the stabiliser in the position of this Tribunal. This stabiliser never reappeared in any of the reports as a piece of evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could the doctor be assisted with the electronic pen and could she be asked to mark the place and the shape of the fracture that you have just discussed. Can you do it in both images and can you use the blue pen, please.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please put today's date and initial the images.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the images be admitted as a separate document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D3550, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Scroll up the page, please. The image is not marked by any particular number.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what you conclude.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there is a number, 108.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I can't see the number.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Below the capital letters, or rather, big letters of the title.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Oh, yes, now I can see it. Go ahead. What do these figures depict? Which stabiliser are these? How do they differ? What do they depict? What do the yellow lines denote?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are stabilisers that were found in the photo file on the left-hand side, that is. In the middle there is a -- stabilisers which exist in this Tribunal and is in evidence and we made geometrical comparisons based on the characteristics which are constant in a shell. And it was established that the stabiliser whose image was found in the photo file and in the video-clip which is on the right-hand side based on the position of the openings for fixing the charge with regard to the fins is the same stabiliser. However, it was also demonstrated that the stabiliser that is at this Tribunal is not the stabiliser from the video-clip and the one whose photo is in the photo file. This was confirmed in another way which is shown in image 109.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Image 109, please. On line 17 there is a word missing, but I suppose this will be corrected when the whole transcript is reviewed.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can see that in the photo file this is not a piece of evidence in the courtroom. The stabiliser is on the video-clip. The position with regard to the series of charge is limited, and if this is branded during the manufacture and with regard to the position of the tail fins, it is very clear that this stabiliser in the courtroom is not actually the stabiliser that was depicted in the photo file and in the video material that was recorded by the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: With regard to the position of the holes, can this be changed simultaneously without using any force?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Once this is fixed, it remains fixed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And now can we go to image 110. Could you please tell us what is the significance of stabiliser number 13?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the stabiliser we have already discussed. It was marked but it was never mentioned during the investigation either by our investigators or CSB investigators or UNPROFOR investigators or any others that were involved in the investigations of this incident and establishing physical evidence at Markale market. As we can see, it is also far from the place of the incident; however, we have also noticed that this stabiliser is more or less on the azimuth or the same line of the shells that had fallen on the square in front of the theatre. I can't establish a link in any case. That's the same direction, the same line, the same azimuth, as it were. And it is clear that the shell could not have two stabilisers that had ended up in the same place.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: However, the theatre is over 200 metres away?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed it is. However, what I'm saying is that this stabiliser was 20 or 30 metres away just like the other one, but it is on the pavement in the direction that corresponds to the other direction or trajectory. However, it could not belong to any of the mines that had exploded there. When it comes to the presence of the stabiliser at the point of incident, I don't have any technical explanation for it, save for a possibility that somebody may have brought it here from somewhere else.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In your view, what happened at Markale? And when it comes to the number and names of the casualties, would that be of any assistance for you to draw your conclusions? I'm talking about Markale 2. What happened during that incident?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see, it's much easier to say what didn't happen during this incident than what did. Based on the traces, the evidence, and the technical capabilities of the shell and the system which was used to detect the trajectory from the VRS positions towards Sarajevo, and based on the testimonies of over 72 people who were interviewed as well as based on the statements provided by those who were present at check-points, we can claim the following: The shell did not possess technical capabilities to fall at the place of the incident without having been caught on radar. It also didn't have any technical capabilities to have been launched from the place alleged by the investigators of the international community because if it had been fired from there, it would have been caught on radar, first of all. And second of all, if that had been the trajectory that they defined it would have ended up on the roof. Based on the traces found in front of the market, it is abundantly clear that the launching had taken place at best with the standard charge. We can say that this may have taken place from the positions under the control of the BiH army, but in that case I believe that the moment when the shell was fired would have been heard. Another thing that we can say that it is certain that those four shells had nothing whatsoever to do with this particular incident. There are some technical ambiguities; for example, the presence of two stabilisers, the difference between the stabiliser that was handed over to the Tribunal as evidence which is part of the technical documentation, and the others. There is a stabiliser there which clearly shows signs of erosion for which there is no explanation. There are many other technical indicators; for example, the impact on the vicinity of the incident in terms of the shattered glass pallet caused injuries for which we don't have any technical explanation with regard to the shell which impacted the area here, i.e., the 120-millimetre mortar shell.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Dr. Subotic. I have no further questions for you during my examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the report be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll receive it. Yes, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mr. President, at page 25 of the English version of the report there's a CV of an individual who's not named as an author of the report, and the CV does not appear in the B/C/S version of the report. So it might be that the CV has been placed there in error or it might be that it did, in fact, have something to do with the compilation of this report.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, may I say something? When it comes to my -- or rather, my colleague Vracaric's CV there is a mistake. It was omitted intentionally. We had a preliminary version that we drafted and we wanted to analyse something from Mr. Berko's analysis with regard to Markale 1. Those were technological considerations of a meteorologist about the fragmentation and his comments that accompanied his analysis. However, we omitted that part of the report and our colleague Vracaric's CV has been kept by mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So that page should be redacted. And also I --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- request the CLSS to upload the images or figures that appear on the original on to the English versions as well. With that caveat we'll receive this.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D3551, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. We'll take a break after which we'll hear the cross-examination. We'll resume at 20 past 1.00. --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.36 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So what's the division of work between you and Ms. Gustafson, Mr. Gaynor?

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Your Honours, I will be cross-examining the witness on the mortar incident report, and Mr. Gaynor will be cross-examining on the Markale report and the air bombs report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. So you'll start, Ms. Gustafson?

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Ms. Subotic. And just before we begin so I know how I should address you, I notice that Dr. Karadzic referred to you as Dr. Subotic. I didn't see a doctoral degree in your CV. I see that you have a masters -- a bachelors and a masters in science. The masters is referred to as a "magistar nauka" - pardon my pronunciation - in Serbian. So is it -- would it be -- how should I address you?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I hold a masters degree in science which my CV says, so you can address me as such. I don't know why they have addressed me as they did.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Subotic. That's helpful. Now, on Sunday when we met, and I'd like to thank for agreeing to meet with myself and Mr. Gaynor in advance of your testimony, we asked you about the fact that your -- the three reports that you've been discussing in your testimony are all co-authored by one or more individuals. And you explained that you collaborated with the other listed authors in your reports but that you were the primary author of these three reports; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And you confirmed to us that regardless of the contributions of others, you stand by all the conclusions in those three reports; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have confirmed this to you. Perhaps I should clarify some of the doubts that may have arisen during the interview when I told you that they co-operated with me. That implies that we collected the materials together, analysed it, dismissed what in our opinion should not be included in the findings and opinion, but I was the one who wrote it, of course with their assistance. So there are no special sections or parts that were written by separate persons while compiling the report. We were simply associates during the preparation and work covering the extensive materials. Personally I'm of the view that whoever participates in some work should be listed or assigned. This is usual when projects like this are handled, what I could have seen in the Galic case. My Professor Stamatovic [phoen], and his assistant Colonel Viritic [phoen], and my colleague Mr. Vukasinovic also were all three listed as the authors of a similar report.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I'd like to move on to another topic. The central axis method of crater analysis - and again we discussed this a little bit when we met - this is the --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not hear you well because I couldn't hear what you were saying.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Okay. I'll start again.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: The evidence in this case indicates that in general the investigations into shell impacts that were carried out at the time utilised what is known as the central axis method, and this is where the two outer edge edges of the shrapnel traces on the side where they're more pronounced are drawn back to the centre of the crater. The angle they create is then bisected with what is called the central axis and that the bearing of that central axis is measured to determine the incoming direction of the shell. Now, you agree that the central axis method that I just described is the standard accepted method of determining the direction of fire of an incoming shell; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just have to say that I'm not sure whether you are saying what I received as the interpretation. I will repeat what you said so that it would be stated correctly. First, the description you provided is technically incorrect, at least in the interpretation that I received. It is the following: The end points of the impression made by the fragments at the moment of the explosion are the end points which are marked by the left and right fork, and the axis of the angle is the bearing which marks the direction of the shell because -- is that what you wanted to ask me? Because co-ordinates were mentioned and I cannot turn the co-ordinates into the angle. So excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Maybe there was some confusion in the translation because I didn't mention co-ordinates. So I think we're more or less on the same page. The -- you said the end points of the impression made by the fragments are the end points which are marked by the left and the right fork. So you have two end points, you use sticks or lines to bring them to the centre of the crater, and then the line that bisects those two end points is the direction from which the shell came?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The line which bisects the angle is the incoming trajectory of the shell.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And you would agree that unless you have a specialised radar system designed to determine the origin of a projectile, that this central axis method is the most accurate and reliable method to determine the incoming trajectory?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The accuracy of the method is defined with a margin of error of plus/minus 10 degrees or 5 depending on the traces on the ground, but generally speaking according to the literature the accuracy of the method is plus/minus 10 degrees. So it can be used for an approximate determination of an incoming trajectory. So the accuracy is plus/minus 10 degrees. That's what the method can yield in terms of results.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Okay. I understand that you are acknowledging that there is a margin of error with these determinations, but my question was more that this -- this is the best way to determine the incoming trajectory of the shell unless you have a radar system to do so; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true that it is an approximative method and the investigators on the ground did not have a better one at their disposal. When I talked to you, I told you that the method was conceived to be used during the war in order to establish approximately when a shell is coming from somewhere so that a commander of a unit, a commanding officer, could assess where the projectile that they were hit with had arrived from so that he could return fire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: But, Doctor, is it the best way in the absence of radar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is an approximate method with the accuracy that I mentioned, with a deviation of between 5 to 10 degrees. That's the margin of error. Because, as I repeat, it all depends on the location where a shell lands. Sometimes the impression is really good, sometimes not, and simply there is another element that affects the accuracy and that is the subjective assessment of the person who is doing this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: But it isn't simply a question of azimuth; it's also a question of range, isn't it? A radar will give you a back plot which assists in the range. But simply seeing the direction of fire will -- may give you an approximate azimuth of fire but it won't assist you as to the range for return fire?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is certainly correct. In this way, only the direction can be determined. The incoming trajectory and approximately if the crater is a good one, then on the basis of the ellipses which it left then very approximately the angle of descent can also be determined. You can see that in various incidents this method was used both by the CSB and some other participants in investigations, namely, determining approximately the angle of descent. And yes, it's also correct that the radar determines the incoming trajectory and also the place from which a shell was launched. And that is why the radar is part of the contemporary equipment of units, perhaps not units that we are talking about here, but a bigger artillery system certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: All the Bench is involved in questions. Ms. Subotic, I don't think you answered the question by Judge Baird. Is there a better method in the absence of radar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, there is no better method when there is no radar, but this method does have its degree of accuracy, if that's an answer that satisfies you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Your answer to Judge Baird's question is yes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And Ms. Subotic, you'd also agree that over time, as time passes, the shrapnel marks in the ground caused by the exploding projectile will erode and deteriorate and it will become harder to identify those marks on the surface and harder to distinguish those marks from other marks that may be on the surface; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In principle, that is so. However, no serious investigator would ever work with traces that are not reliable and that do not provide a degree of accuracy to his or her results. So that's quite true. Erosion due to the weather conditions and the time that elapses certainly affects the traces, but let me repeat no investigator would, I suppose, use traces that are not reliable.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And the crater itself, the crater formed by the falling projectile, that will also erode due to weather and human traffic, and it will become harder to determine the central point of the crater as time passes; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And because of these factors, the ideal time to conduct a crater analysis would be immediately after the explosion, when the marks are fresh, the crater is fresh, and that's when you're most likely to get the best and most reliable results; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's certainly true and I said that in the courtroom that that's the usual practice of forensic technicians, that whenever an incident occurs, whether in war time or in peace time, first of all, the place of the incident, the site, is secured and then so that no traces would be jeopardised an on-site investigation is conducted. So you're absolutely right and that is the practice in forensic technical investigation, that nothing should be moved at the site so that the conclusions would be correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And in terms of analysing crater impacts in person versus through photographs, it's also -- there are some disadvantages, I would suggest, through analysing photographs. For example, if the photograph is taken at any distance there will be perspective issues. It's more difficult to determine angles. You're also limited by the distance of the photograph. You can't actually go and examine the traces up close. Factors like that will make crater analysis on a photograph more difficult than one conducted in person; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true in principle, but you disregarded one contemporary technology which allows for each such photograph to be placed in a vertical position by computer analysis, and thereby remove the angle from which it was filmed and deformations caused by the photography that can all be removed. And thanks to the new techniques which are now available, especially computer analysis, it's possible to remove that. So generally speaking you are right, unless we also take into account this: Namely, that we use it as something that is needed and necessary. Of course we try to make sure that any investigation is not burdened with such elements because then we'll be more accurate and more reliable.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Okay. But even if you have this technology available, you still can only see what's on the photograph. You can't get any closer than the photograph to examine the traces, whereas if in person you would be able to go as close as you like to examine the shrapnel and the crater, and that would assist the analysis; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and we noticed the difference when we went out into the field and found the traces which we could then examine from close up. So you are right.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And in -- on that note, you explained to us on Sunday that you were not in Bosnia during the war, certainly not in Sarajevo during the war, and the first time you went to the locations of these incidents to examine the incident sites was in 2010; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is true. I did not visit the incident sites before that occasion and I was not in Bosnia during the war, nor at the incident sites in the Sarajevo area. So that is true.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: So it follows then that all the crater analyses you've done for your various reports are conducted -- were -- sorry, were conducted either on the basis of these visits to the sites in 2010 or later, or on the basis of photographs or video stills of the sites or some combination of those. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And you also told us on Sunday that although you had learned the methodology of the central axis method during your studies, that it was not part of your job at the Belgrade Technical Institute to conduct crater analyses and that in your 35 years of employment at the institute you had not conducted a crater analysis; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, though I am obliged to explain what the matter is here. The analysis of the craters was made on the basis of the basic principle, the absolutely basic principles. It's unimaginable that someone doesn't know them and did complete the sort of school that I have and was of the same profession as me. What I said on Sunday is that such analysis is only done in case of war, and they're intended primarily for military units so that they could make an approximate assessment as to the places from which they were fired at. And the analysis of this kind is made primarily for them and at the military technical institute we had no need to do that sort of analysis for the simple reason that we were not at war and we did not have such craters to analyse. So, excuse me, these are elementary things which are taught, and it's unimaginable that someone who has reached his third year of university studies would not know this and precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Okay. So is it right then that the only crater analyses you have conducted are the ones you did for the purposes of your report or reports? Sorry.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: So then it's right as well that you have never in your life conducted a crater analysis on a freshly formed crater in person; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, I have to remember. Perhaps during one of the experiments we did do such an analysis. I really can't remember now. It's possible that during some of the experiments at the training-ground in Nikinci we did analyse that if, for example, one of our projectiles deflected from its trajectory, but I can't remember because even if we did do it then it was such an unimportant analysis that I can't even recall it.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Okay. It's clear from your CV and your publications that you have significant experience in the area of ballistics, but I don't see anything in your CV about any publications in the area of crime scene investigations. You haven't published in the area of crime scene investigation, have you?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct. That's not correct. In my CV there are more than 100 findings which were made for courts, and in each of these I did visit the crime scene. I don't know how you missed that.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: All right. But that was for -- those related to specialised findings in ballistics. But in terms of general crime scene analysis, that's not an area that you've published in, general crime scene analysis techniques or processes?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: General or whatever, but there are 105 findings on expert analysis listed here, and in each of these I visited the crime scene in order to be able to write the report. And there are also several papers that have legal elements. I wrote them for legal journals. One of them that I remember is the determination of the place from which a projectile was launched on the basis of an audio-recording on an answering machine of the damaged party when they shot at him from three different directions and he was at home. The report is listed here and I think that it was published at least in two legal journals and also presented at a conference. I remember that in particular. Therefore, several papers that are linked with the investigations and ballistic expert analysis conducted on the crime scene, and I suppose that you have seen the one report here and also the list of the expert reports that had to be drawn up for the needs of courts. In each case, I have to visit a crime scene because what is usual in our parts is that when the investigating judge goes out to the scene, he calls the expert to accompany him for the reason that it might happen that not all the necessary traces which are important for determining this are recorded. And that's the particular aspect and that -- those are the on-site investigations conducted by relevant experts at the crime scene.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could now go to your report on the mortar incidents, which is D3542. Just so you're aware, Ms. Subotic, I'm going to start with incident G5, which is the 12th of July, 1993, incident at the water-line where the 82-millimetre mortar round struck. And the reason I'm going to start with that one is because this is one that I'll go through in a bit more detail than the others, although I'm limited in my time so I can't cover everything. And then we'll go back through the scheduled incidents in order and I will cover the other ones in somewhat less detail. Now, according to your report your position for this incident is that the shell in this case could --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a second, please, so I can find it in the hard copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Paragraph 49.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you. [Interpretation] I have found it in the meantime. It's easier for me to recognise it on the basis of the figures or images.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: So your position here is that the shell could not have been fired from the west/north-west, which is what the contemporaneous investigations concluded. You conclude that the shell was fired from the north/north-east, and that conclusion can be found in paragraph 62(g). Now, I'd like to start with -- at paragraph 56, which is page 82 in the B/C/S and page 37 in the English. And here you note that the --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Paragraph 56?

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. You note here that the investigation file, which is P1438 in this case, states that at 1515 the police warned the citizens not to loiter in the area because the nearest confrontation lines were 200 metres away. And you conclude that since none of the witnesses testified that there had ever been such a warning before that this leads to the conclusion that the police had been tipped off in advance that a shell would be fired. And I'd like to ask you a couple of questions about that. The evidence you refer to simply indicates that the police warned people in the area not to loiter. The evidence doesn't say one way or another whether the police had given such warnings on other occasions; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not stated here; however, the police issued a similar warning in the event of the incident of the 4th of February when humanitarian aid was being distributed. At that time the police also issued a warning that people should not gather at the plateau because shelling was anticipated to take place there -- was expected to take place there. So there were other such instances. This is not an isolated case.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Well, the witness you actually cite here in footnote 201 and this is witness AE from the Galic case did say that the police had warned them that day not to queue in the area and witness AE confirmed that there was a risk, and the risk was: "The risk concerned you leaving your house every day. You could be killed." And this is at transcript pages 6021 to 6022 of the Galic trial. And the evidence in this case confirms that there was a great deal of shelling in Dobrinja. And I would refer to Dzevlan at page 11750. So, Ms. Subotic, in the circumstances where the area of Dobrinja was coming under regular shell fire it's logical, is it not, that the police would warn people not to loiter in the area and this doesn't even begin to suggest that the police were tipped off that this particular shell would be launched, does it?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First, I wish to say that Dobrinja was not shelled. Rather, from what I could gather from the documents there was fighting going on there. There was evidence of the fighting having taken place there and that this was not the result of shelling but rather the result of fighting where shells landed from all quarters. So that's not correct. And all the evidence shows that this was exactly the case. That's number one. Number two, let me say that it is quite odd - and we did write it down and it wasn't an explicit assertion - but we did notice that several minutes earlier people were warned and then a shell landed, and that afterwards it took a very long time before the CSB was contacted and called to conduct an investigation. I think that it was quite a long time after the event, as far as I remember from this report. So it's not an explicit statement. It was merely an indication of a possibility.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Okay. You said: "First, I wish to say that Dobrinja was not shelled." Are you disputing the eye-witness testimony in this case that shells fell in the Federation-held parts of Sarajevo, in Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, far from it. Now, when you say that Dobrinja was shelled from the perspective of my profession this is the way it would appear: I am somewhere on the side and shelling this Tribunal non-stop and you are sitting there doing nothing. This is the distinction that I want to draw. I am not disputing the statements that shells fell; rather, what I'm saying is that on the basis of the evidence that we had, it was visible that what was at play was some sort of fighting. So this is the issue of my professional view and the way of how what you said was interpreted to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Okay. I'd like to now turn to paragraph 58, the next paragraph, where you discuss the UNPROFOR report on this incident. And if we could pull that up, it's P1442. And it is your position that UNPROFOR received from the local investigators information about the type and calibre of shell, number of casualties, time of the explosion, et cetera. And then at paragraph 62(g) you go a bit further and you state that it is clear that the UNPROFOR report and the Bosnian report used the same data. And you conclude that these were not two independent reports whose results match. And I don't think it's disputed that these two reports, P1438 which is the CSB report and P1442, the UNPROFOR report, do have matching results that the shell flew in from the west/north-west. So if we go to page 2 of this document and the subject is crater analysis mortar attack. And then under crater characteristics it says: "The form of the spray shows the direction of 5100 mils west/west-north." And as I think you point out in your report, 5100 mils is 287 degrees --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Now, it does go on to say that the 82-millimetre mortar shell fin found at the site was given to the crater analysis officer by local officials, but on its face this report indicates that on the key issue of the trajectory of the shell UNPROFOR conducted its own analysis and drew its own conclusions on the trajectory; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is certainly what would appear on the basis of what is written here; however, I continue to stand by the statement that we were saying, after all, that they did not have at their disposal the stabiliser itself to review it because as far as I was able to glean from the documents the stabiliser had been handed over to the CSB for analysis. And on the other hand it is impossible for two analyses to be fully consistent. You were able to see that we analysed something that was very exact and yet the difference between our analysis and the analysis of those who were there at the time was of several degrees. I stand by my view that these were not independent reports, especially because --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the witness please repeat what she said.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And it is quite -- it is not to be expected at all that people would not be exchanging their information --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Interpreters didn't hear you, in particular at the end of your answer. Could you repeat from, "I stand by my view ..."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that it cannot particularly be concluded explicitly that it was done jointly or not. So it -- one cannot conclude either that they conducted the investigation independently or jointly. However, the investigation was conducted simultaneously and the data indicate that the stabiliser -- handed over the stabiliser, or rather, the CSB handed over the stabiliser to the KTZ. And of course the stabiliser would have confirmed which shell was active in the incident and that the marks at the scene were atypical because the projectile had been activated at a certain height above the ground in mid-air. Had this been the case, then they would have had to establish what the calibre was. My conclusion was that they exchanged information and that therefore the investigations were not independent.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Okay. On Sunday when we spoke you explained that you comprehensively reviewed the material that the Defence provided to you and that you could access from the internet with respect to these incidents from the Galic trial record. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. You asked me if I had access to the documents that were confidential; that's the way I understood your question. I really don't know that I did have access to a document which was - how do you call it here? - under seal. So I said that I was not aware that I had access to any document that was confidential. And yes, we did use everything that we could gain access to on the Tribunal's site and everything that we received here from you as the supporting documentation from the Prosecution and our team when we were looking for something or when we found something that may shed light on a fact.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Could we move into private session for a moment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Shall the Chamber move into private session briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we are now in open session, Ms. Gustafson.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Paragraph 60(a), that can be found on page 39 of the English and 85 of the B/C/S. And here, Ms. Subotic, you claim that the --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A moment, please. 60(a)?

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: That's right. It should be page 85.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Now, here you state that the Skoda car that the shell exploded behind was facing south-east rather than east, as you say that Mr. Cavcic, the ballistics expert, stated in his ballistics report. And you state: "This fact is important for the determination of the direction from which the shell was fired." So you seem to be claiming that Mr. Cavcic based his direction of fire determination on the orientation of the car and because the orientation of the car was incorrect his determination of fire was also incorrect. Is that what you're saying here?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Firstly, the orientation of the car has not been erroneously determined. The car is situated in front of the building next to the fence of which the projectile was activated, and it's at an azimuth of 157 which is the east -- south-east.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Sorry, my question I think was a bit confusing. Let me try again. Are you saying that because Mr. Cavcic --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The orientation is not wrong, the orientation of the Skoda. It is parked in the position of the south-east. You can see that at paragraph 43 and at figure 60(a), or rather, figure 44.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Sorry. I think my question was a little confusing, so I'm going to try again. I think what you are saying here is that Mr. Cavcic wrongly stated that the direction of the Skoda -- that the Skoda was facing east, when in fact as you point out it was facing south-east. Because he got that wrong and he based his -- and you also -- I think you're concluding that he based his determination of the direction of fire on his determination of the direction of the car, and because the direction of the car was stated erroneously, the direction of fire was also erroneous. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, from the beginning to the end. First of all, it wasn't on the basis of the orientation of the car and the car's position that Mr. Cavcic determined the direction of fire. First of all, this isn't something that he did in his document. He explained in detail the way in which he determined it. I'm sorry, it must have been down to the translation that you concluded what you just said in your question. None of the things stand this way. Mr. Cavcic determined the incoming trajectory the way he described it here and in his testimony, and we did relate it here in detail, but I didn't relate it in this way nor did I think that it was because of this reason that his conclusion was wrong. His conclusion was erroneous primarily because it lies on a number of assumptions which are not correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Okay. Because the reason I ask is because you have cited to Mr. Cavcic's ICTY witness statement in your discussion of this incident, and that's footnotes 210 and 215. And in that statement Mr. Cavcic specified that when he made determinations of direction of fire he used a compass. So if he used a compass, as he said he did in his statement, then whatever he said about the orientation of the car wouldn't matter because he made his determination based on the analysis of the marks and a compass; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to underline again that his statement about the orientation of the car had nothing to do with his determination of the actual direction of fire, the direction from which the shell flew in, nor was it taken as a parameter to challenge this conclusion. So the orientation of the car, regardless of how he described it in his report, was not taken as one of the reasons why his conclusion would be considered erroneous. The way in which we determined the direction of fire was on the basis of physical evidence and the tenets of the profession that we belonged to, which is presented here in detail.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you. That's clear now. Now I'd like to turn now to your determination of the direction of fire. So, first of all, you agree that you were at a couple of disadvantages vis-a-vis the people who investigated this incident at the time. Firstly, the only physical evidence that still remains at the scene are the remains of shrapnel damage to the asphalt which you examined in 2010, so 17 years after the incident. So not only is the shrapnel damage -- it has weathered over 17 years, but also you were not able to examine in person the shrapnel damage to the car or the fence which the contemporaneous investigations took into account; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot agree with you. I can agree on specific points, but not with your entire question. Under 1, as far as the shrapnel marks on the asphalt are concerned, they are very well preserved, as can be seen in the photograph that we submitted. Under 2, if we observed the photographs from the photo file, you will agree that the photo file was produced on the day, in other words, not later after items were removed and the crime scene was tampered with and that it was clearly put together. Now, if you put the car back in the position where it was and if you look at the various directions from which the deformations were produced, it's completely clear how the shock wave acted, from which side it acted, and in what way. It was on the basis of these very good photographs that one could determine at which height the explosion took place. In particular, one could determine the position of the stabiliser ahead of the rear right tire of the car, which could not possibly have ended up there had the shell flown in from the direction that the investigators and Mr. Cavcic determined. Let me not name each and every one of them, but they are physical marks. This is physical evidence that was established at the moment it happened. So it isn't deformation we're talking about. We're talking about the main trajectory. We're not talking about whether the trajectory was 5 degrees to the left or 5 degrees to the right. We're talking about the trajectory which is physically impossible if it was to happen the way the investigators said it did. It was especially -- it is especially unacceptable if you read what Mr. Cavcic wrote, and I'm sure you will be able to find the relevant part, that all the evidence and marks that he was able to retrieve he established all converged on the hip of the injured person. And we all know that the person could not possibly have been in that position where all these imaginary lines of his converged. Because had the shell flown in the way these investigators imagined that it did, that person could not possibly have been there.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise if I was too fast for the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Just to go back to something you said earlier in your answer, you said that: "As far as the shrapnel marks on the asphalt are concerned, they are very well preserved." Now, earlier you said that you had never conducted a crater analysis on a freshly formed crater except possibly once at a firing range but it was so unimportant you can no longer remember. So it's difficult for you to say how well preserved the shrapnel marks are when you've never really analysed an incident where the shrapnel marks are fresh; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. You have to bear in mind that I have examined a great deal of projectiles for their fragmentation effect. I know exactly what the shrapnel acts -- what it does to the surface. We had never tested a projectile without knowing what its fragment would do, and this is something that we would do in our testing rounds. So I did investigate the effect in this way. However, there is one thing that I have to say. The mark is either discernible and clear, or it is not visible and not clear. What we found on the ground was marks that were very visible and clear. We marked them ourselves. They had a defined arc which you can see -- or a curve which you can see on the figure there. And to illustrate the direction, which I repeat, we did not determine as a specific figure but as an approximation. And I do believe that this is what is written in our report. I say "we," because my associate Poparic and myself were there as well as with an entire team of Bosnian policemen. We were all there.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: In line 22 it should be written "we had never developed any projectile without testing," "developed" is out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Ms. Subotic, you said the mark is either visible and clear or it is not visible and not clear. Now, my point is that if the mark is not visible and not clear because it's been on an asphalt surface for 17 years, eroding and deteriorating and being weathered, then you didn't see it and you didn't mark it; right? And you don't know whether there were marks that were no longer visible and not clear, do you?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We marked, or rather, your question is hypothetical. Whatever we saw, all the visible traces, we marked. They can also be seen in photo files, on photos that were taken 17 years later. They do not differ in terms of their positioning. What we marked and what we did was much more correct than if we had done it based on a photo that is exactly identical. If you look at the photo file of the crime prevention services, you will see that those traces are absolutely identical in terms of their distribution and positioning after 17 years. We did not add a single one and we did not ignore any that we saw. It is possible that we did not see some of them because of the lapse of time; however, there was a sufficient number to enable us to confirm that what we found in the photo file was accurate and the photo file was available and accessible to both you and a me.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go then to page 88 of your report. And you've just --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I'd like to look at the figure, so if you could just go to page 88.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well then.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Now you've -- in your answer you've placed a lot of emphasis on the fact that the marks in the photo file were identical to the ones you saw when you visited the scene. So if we could zoom in on the photo on the left-hand side. Now, this is -- you've marked here with white circles what you consider to be the shrapnel marks in the asphalt. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And it's clear you've drawn three circles on the sidewalk and one just on the edge of the sidewalk, end of road. Now, if we could bring up side by side to this page 93 of your report, in particular figure 52. And if we could zoom in on the middle of the photo on the right-hand side and slide it over so we can see what's on the right-hand side. Now, in this photograph you've again marked in with circles what you could see in terms of shrapnel marks in 2010, and it's clear that there are on the order of 20 shrapnel marks identified on the sidewalk here. So we've got three shrapnel marks on the sidewalk when you marked the photo and roughly 20 when you went to the scene. So these are not consistent at all, in fact. Your shrapnel markings on these two -- on the photo versus what you saw in 2010 are totally inconsistent; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not correct, no. Look here, we did not do our job to illustrate every single piece of shrapnel for you based on those that we found in photo file. From here I can see the traces that we did not mark on the left-hand side photo. We didn't consider that we had to do it. We did not look for the consistency of the two findings of the site of explosion. From here I can see at least 15 traces on the pavement that we did not mark. This was marked only to show the trajectory or either the main curve is marked, not every shrapnel trace. If we zoomed in on this photo, if we were to mark every single piece of shrapnel, there would be an exact match. If it's of any interest to you, I can do it for tomorrow and I can in that case perhaps do away with your dilemma.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Sorry, Ms. Subotic, correct me if I am wrong but your line number 4 in figure 46 is the line that you claim is the middle of the arc of the shrapnel that you have marked in this photograph; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's just the approximate trajectory. It's not the middle of the arc. This is what we marked. However, this is just the approximation of the trajectory within which all the traces fit, especially the traces on the Skoda car that we saw from the back. You can understand that the analysis of a crater of this kind is not a classical analysis because the shell was activated at 65 centimetres above the ground so the arc cannot be typical of what we are accustomed to when we analyse similar craters.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Ms. Subotic, at paragraph 40 -- sorry, 60(d), and this is at the bottom of page 41 in the English, you state with respect to the photo on the left: "In order to clarify this vital detail in figure 45, the visible damage to the asphalt has been marked white on figure 46. This makes it easy to observe the regular pattern characteristic for the fragmentation of a shell." And then you say this is a partial representation of fragmentation because the shell exploded at a height above the surface. And you say: "Yet it allows us to determine the direction from which the shell had come in with some accuracy. This direction is marked in figure 46 with a yellow line 4." Now what you said there is quite categoric and it is contradictory to what you said a few moments ago about this being an approximate trajectory based on some but not all of the shrapnel marks visible in the photo, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps this looked categoric to you, but it says here it may be concluded with reliability that the direction of -- from which the projectile arrived was north or slightly eastwards. This is just an approximation and I report this is not the exact angle to the millimetre. Do you understand? We know that the curve is 157 and I suppose that all of us see here that the angle is left to the curve 157, and if we look at Google Earth you will see that it is either north or a bit eastward and we are talking about the place of launch and not the place where the shell landed.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Okay. Sorry, I'm going to move on in a moment but before we do you claimed that you could see additional shrapnel marks on the sidewalk on this photo. So I'd like to zoom in on the photo in figure 46 and have you mark these shrapnel markings that you claim are visible here. And I think you said there were at least 15 of them.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would Madam Gustafson agree the markings to be put on the left-hand side which was not done before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And can the photo please zoomed in on a bit more, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Ms. Subotic, if you'd like the photo to be zoomed in, that can be done, because once we move the photo the markings disappear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's zoom in further.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is enough. This is enough. Thank you. You don't have to zoom in any further. Very well now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Would you wait.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I?

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Just to remind you at line 15 of page 91 you said: "From here I can see at least 15 traces on the pavement that we did not mark."

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would very much like to delete the last trace I marked. So you want me to mark only the traces on the pavement?

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Well, that's what you asserted you could see, so the ones on the pavement -- yes, on the sidewalk that you can see.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You wanted to delete something?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I may have not been very precise when I made my circles, but it's really neither here nor there, is it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Can I now continue drawing?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If you could put your signature and the date, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll receive it as a Prosecution Exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P6319, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Ms. Gustafson, before you continue, because I may not get another chance to ask these questions, there are a series of short questions I'd like to put to the witness at this point. The first is a general one: Have you ever been to the scene of a mortar explosion in the minutes after it detonated where injury or death was occasioned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Just the testing grounds where we examined mortar shells. It was there that I saw quite a huge number of such detonations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Yes. I was particularly asking with reference to the injuries caused. The second question - these questions are not definitive and they're not designed to stop either Ms. Gustafson or Mr. Gaynor from asking or expanding on them, it's just that I'd like them to be on the record - do you agree that a mortar round can have an impact fuse with immediate effect or delayed fuse, where the -- a detonation doesn't take place for a set period after impact?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you're right. All mortar rounds have fuses with immediate effect. Each of the fuses in question has a safety pin which is connected to certain inertia and it is primarily used to prevent such projectiles to be activated at the beginning of their trajectory and to protect the launching crew. Is this what you have asked me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: No. That is something that we've already heard. What I'm asking is: Do you know or accept that there are mortar fuses which detonate upon immediate impact and some fuses which are initiated upon impact but the detonation doesn't occur until a variable time afterwards depending on the nature of the delay fuse?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As a matter of fact, I did answer your question. All mortar rounds in our country are fitted with a so-called UTI fuses which are contact fuses, which means that they have an immediate action but there is a safety pin that protects the crew at the beginning of trajectory. Our 82- and 120-millimetre rounds have that kind of fuses. There are all sorts of fuses and they are fitted to all sorts of rounds in accordance with the requirements of the tactical authority. You are right, there are such things, but our 82- and 102-mortar [as interpreted] rounds are fitted with the so-called UTI fuses which is the abbreviation that stands for a contact fuse and it has exactly the properties that I have explained just now.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's be of some assistance with the interpretation. The UTI, what is this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the contact inertia fuse. The inertia applies to the safety clause that I mentioned in -- earlier in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: I think we all understood that. Thank you. Going on to explosive effect, explosives can create both blast and vacuum, can't they, so that sometimes an explosion will cause, for instance, next to a building debris to be injected into the building and sometimes the vacuum effect of explosive, depending on how far it is away, will have a sucking-out effect of debris. Would you agree with that proposition?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, I did not understand the interpretation very well. I don't know what the debris may be in this case, or at least the word that was used for the word "debris" is not clear to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Well, irrespective of the debris, there can be explosions which have the effect of creating a vacuum into which debris is drawn, i.e., towards the explosive. There are also instances where an explosion pushes debris away from the point of detonation in the opposite direction. Both phenomena can be observed in some explosions. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. May I be of assistance? If the Doctor received the interpretation fragments, meaning shell fragments, there is no inertia that would pull them towards the centre. I would say debris, the material fragments from the ground, from the point of impact. That's what I would use.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: I'm not talking about fragments of the shell casing. I'm talking about external material. It can have both effects. Do you agree with that proposition?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have to be certain that I understand you properly. You're saying that under certain conditions when there is a detonation or an explosion within an environment which is defined in geometrical terms, a vacuum can be created and that it can cause an unexpected movement of bricks, for example, or certain parts of that kind that may be found in the vicinity. Is this the gist of your question? Did I understand you properly?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Yes, in other words debris can be brought towards the point of detonation by the vacuum effect?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These would be very specific conditions and these conditions are defined by the point of impact and the area where the detonation takes place. When a detonation happens in a large open space or at least an open space this is quite improbable or impossible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Well, I'll leave for others to develop that if they wish. I'm just talking about the general principle. The other matter I want to deal with is secondary debris. You talked about injuries caused by the fragmentation of the casing of a mortar bomb. Did you take into account when looking at the photographs of the injuries the possibility of injuries caused by debris that was blown by the force of the explosion into the victim as opposed to the shell casing or shrapnel itself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we are looking at the injuries that happened on the 28th of May and that major lesion, I didn't take into account the possibility of injuring due to debris in the form of a large object. That was a possibility. However, there was no blood under the injured person that may have corroborated that theory and justified such a large injury in such a place. Having said that, you are right, that injury may have been caused by a stone or the -- a grenade. In any case, a secondary debris of larger proportions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Did you say 28th of May?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was Markale 2, was it the 28th of May?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: August.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, it was in August indeed. I have a lot of problems with the dates because there were a number of incidents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Well, I think we all understand what you meant. And the last question I want to pose is this: If an explosive charge, for instance, an artillery shell or a mortar round, is detonated remotely, i.e., not by impact but being detonated remotely, that is going to require a device to be attached to the mortar round or to the shell and a primary -- and an explosive charge in order to cause the secondary detonation. That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. And the initial action had to be over, the fuse had to be eliminated and that's what is the initial part of its construction. In order to be activated, it has to achieve a distance, and then it can be activated. That's why I said it was the initial action and that initial part has to be blocked in that fuse. And then what you mentioned can occur subsequently. So one action has to precede the other.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: And therefore, unless it is vapourised, there is going to be the opportunity at least for physical evidence of that secondary device that's been attached to the bomb or the mortar round to be found at or near the scene?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that should be the case. It should be found in the vicinity. If we're talking about certain specific devices. If it's not a TNT round which doesn't leave traces, a Trotyl round is just a piece of TNT which contains the detonating casing and that does not leave any traces. It explodes together with the mother shell.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Transcript, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On page 98, line 17, when the stone is mentioned and that is a stone that would have been projected by a shell. On 99 "armoured" was not properly interpreted. This is the initial arming of the shell. I hope that Your Excellencies understood that. The Doctor said that when speed is achieved the shell is armoured, i.e., the initial fuse is prepared for explosion and I can't see that recorded in the Doctor 's answer. And on line 17 she said that it could be a rifle grenade or a brick, anything that was pushed or projected by the explosion. If we have the time, maybe you should ask the witness to explain what armouring is, why this happens, and what she said about the stone or a piece of brick.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm convinced that everybody here have already mastered the terminology because we have been discussing the same things for a long time, but in any case let me try. The professional term for making the fuse capable of initiating an explosion is called armouring. When we say the inertia contact fuse means that the fuse is restricted or limited before it is armoured, i.e., before it is brought to a state where it can initiate the explosion. In technical terms this was resolved in the following way: Once a speed of flying is achieved together with inertia, the fuse is released and it can be activated. I also mentioned that we are primarily talking about the reasons of safety of the crew which launches such projectiles.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll stop here for today. Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I'll be brief. As the Court must be aware, the accused took about four times the estimated period for his examination-in-chief, consuming an almost extra two days. Not surprisingly, that had an impact on the upcoming schedule and next week's witnesses in particular. The proposed solution by the Defence has been to submit a revised schedule, but that belatedly revised schedule is quite problematic for the Prosecution. I met immediately with Mr. Robinson to see if we could reach some accommodation that would work for both parties. So far we have not been successful, but it may be the case that the success of our discussions may turn on the availability of extra or extended sessions either tomorrow or next week. So I wanted to bring that to the Court's attention to see if that could at least be explored to see if it's feasible. We'll obviously continue to discuss the matter to see what we can do short of extra or extended sessions. But as I say, that might be an adjustment that might just be sufficient to bridge the gap. And I wanted to raise it in case it could be thrown into the mix. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How much extension do you have in mind when you are talking about tomorrow's hearing?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, I think what we were talking about, as we discussed it, was an extra hour or hour and a half for two of the four days remaining between now and Thursday of next week. At least that was part of our discussion as it took place. We're going to continue to work on it. I presume we may identify some greater specificity or more refinement in what is needed as we do so, but that was the nature of the discussion as it took place thus far.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If either of the parties could e-mail our staff as to this more detailed information so that we can understand more correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll continue tomorrow at 9.00. The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 16th of May, 2013, at 9.00 a.m. 24 25
